subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram expose explicit child forum-topic subagent sessions, or should `thread:true` remain a current-conversation binding by default?
rationale: Current code already supports Telegram session binding, but child-topic creation changes user-visible chat behavior and conflicts with the open issue asking Telegram not to create user-visible threads for internal subagent runs.

options.title: Keep current-conversation default
options.body: Treat current main as the supported Telegram behavior and handle child-topic creation only through a separately approved opt-in design.

options.title: Sponsor child-topic support
options.body: Adopt or replace the open Telegram PR after resolving conflicts, compatibility risks, and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Reject child topics for subagents
options.body: Close the child-topic direction and update docs/tool affordances so Telegram subagent binding is clearly current-conversation only.

recommendation.title: Keep current-conversation default
recommendation.body: Treat current main as the supported Telegram behavior and handle child-topic creation only through a separately approved opt-in design.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the core thread-binding refactor and is the clearest owner for deciding whether the shared binding model should grow a Telegram child-topic affordance.
